🔥🔥🔥🔥

Michael Saylor and Adam Back have publicly opposed Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) 110.

The proposal seeks to reduce spam transactions by altering Bitcoin’s consensus rules. But critics say it won’t fix the core issue—and may open the door to risky precedents.

Saylor argues that spam isn’t Bitcoin’s most pressing threat, and modifying consensus rules for this purpose could lead to unintended long-term consequences. Back contends that BIP 110 undermines Bitcoin’s foundational principles by trying to control how users engage with the network.

Others highlight a recent experiment where a developer embedded a 66 KB image directly into a transaction—effectively circumventing the exact restrictions BIP 110 aims to impose.

The lesson: if someone is determined to store data on Bitcoin, they’ll likely find a workaround. Meaning consensus-level changes may be an ineffective fix.

🔥 @Bitcoin_Insights
